text:
matt: incident-bot auto-page: high OOM and crashloop rate in inference-prod-usw2. Observed rapid node churn and many 503s from the edge. Marking P0 :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Alert #88210 — cuda_oom_rate > 20% in last 5m for inference-prod-usw2. See logs: https://logs.redwood.local/88210

sarah: I'm live on this. ACK and joining triage.

kai: Quick data: repeated CUDA OOM stack in runtime-worker on large-seq requests. Crashloop count spiked after autoscaler added nodes. Replica pods die on first warmup attempt.

jessica: Pod excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T01:52:18Z] runtime-worker: AllocError: CUDA OOM (need 3.2GB, available 1.4GB)
  File "/srv/runtime/worker.py", line 389, in process
    cache.reserve(kv_size)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
```

olivia-research: Pattern: a handful of tenants sending >10k token contexts which bloat KV cache. Autoscaler reacts to higher queue length, scales immediately, but fresh nodes are hit with heavy sessions right away and crash. Thundering herd on warmup.

david: Current scale config: minNodes=10, maxNodes=200, scaleUpWindow=20s, scaleDownWindow=25s, burst=true. Node boot and GPU warmup ~4-6min. Our cool windows are too tight.

matt: Immediate mitigations proposed: 1) mute burst mode on autoscaler, 2) enforce ramp-up window so new nodes get limited traffic for first 6 minutes, 3) route long-context traffic to low-memory model variant. Can infra flip burst off quickly?

david: Applying change: burst=false and scaleUpWindow=300s (5m) for inference-prod-usw2. Pushing change now via infra console. Will also set nodegroup launch template to reserve 2GB host memory for system processes.

kai: In parallel, recommending model fallback: route requests with prompt_tokens > 4096 to quantized model pool (q4_0) and cap per-tenant concurrency for those paths. Olivia — can you push routing rule?

olivia-research: Pushing rule: if prompt_tokens > 4096 OR kv_size > 1e7 -> route to pool quant-q4_0. Also set tenant concurrency cap = 8 for that pool. Deploying to routing service in 60s.

jessica: Temp envoy config to protect nodes (examples):
```
- match: /v1/generate
  headers:
    - name: x-prompt-tokens
  rate_limit:
    requests_per_minute: 30
    concurrent: 8
```
Pushed rate-limit to edge for known long-context endpoints.

sarah: Performing safe drains on the three most-affected nodes. Using extended grace to let in-flight requests finish:
kubectl cordon gpu-node-23
kubectl drain gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=900
david: Also tuning kubelet eviction settings to be less aggressive during this incident (evictionHard memory.available=150Mi -> 50Mi temporarily).

incident-bot: Notifying support and ops channels, paging oncall-sre.

support-bot: Opened customer ticket 95401 for impacted customers in us-west-2. Drafted status message: "Experiencing increased errors in inference in us-west-2; mitigations in progress. No data loss detected."

matt: Quick impact summary for execs/support: ~9-14% of requests to heavy-context endpoints returned 503 or were timed out between 01:30-02:05. Several large tenants hit concurrency caps and saw degraded experience. No integrity/data loss.

kai: After routing change, immediate drop in OOM rate. Pod crashloops fell from 31% -> 4% across the cluster. Quant pool handling heavy contexts without OOMs.

jessica: Also observed some jobs leaking GPU memory across requests — runtime-worker shows sustained RSS growth in some workers. We'll need memory profiler.

olivia-research: Scheduling memprof on runtime-worker; will run isolated repros on a staging group and correlate to tenant prompt patterns.

david: Infra follow-ups queued: reserve host memory in launch template, increase node boot buffer, add guarded ramp (traffic ramp 0 -> 100% over 6 minutes). Creating infra tickets.

support: Initial notices sent to top affected accounts; offered credits per SLA. Monitoring customer responses.

sarah: Handoff to night team in 25m — @mike will own watch and escalation. Current state: autoscaler burst off, scaleUp window increased to 5m, routing in place, rate-limits applied, crashloops reduced.

mike: ACK handoff. Will observe dashboards and watch error budget.

matt: Playbook (for postmortem and runbook updates):
- 1) Disable autoscale burst for impacted GPU clusters when OOM thrash is detected
- 2) Increase scaleUp window to at least node warmup time (>=300s)
- 3) Apply traffic ramping for new nodes for initial N minutes
- 4) Route long-context requests to memory-efficient model variants by default
- 5) Introduce per-tenant concurrency limits for heavy endpoints
- 6) Add runtime memory profiling and leak detection in CI
- 7) Update alert thresholds to correlate OOM rate with scale events to reduce noisy pages

olivia-research: Assigning owners and SLAs:
R1 infra: implement traffic ramp + host reserve (SLA 2w)
R2 runtime: memprof + leak fix (SLA 3d)
R3 product/devex: model-variant default routing + console hint (SLA 1w)
david: Created infra change requests and scheduled a maintenance window for a safer rollout of autoscaler heuristic changes.

incident-bot: Incident 88210 marked Mitigated by matt at 2026-03-15T03:30:00Z. Root cause: autoscaler reacting faster than node warmup time + immediate routing of large-context sessions to fresh GPUs causing CUDA OOMs and crashloops; exacerbated by KV cache spike patterns from a small set of tenants.

matt: Post-incident: blameless postmortem scheduled, runtime & infra to collaborate on warmup and memory fixes. Tagging runtime-team, infra, product, support.

mike: Final watch note: small latency jitter at 03:55 but no customer-facing errors. Monitoring through window until 08:00.

pagerduty: Incident closed. No further pages to oncall-sre.

support: Logging final incident summary to customer portal and adding follow-ups for any escalations.

sarah: Closing the handoff thread. If anything regresses, ping @mike and escalate to the oncall rotation.
